items.stem: What does Horace Danby like to collect ?
items.answer: Horace Danby likes to collect rare and expensive books.

items.stem: Why does he steal every year ?
items.answer: He is a lock maker. He leads a good life. But he steals once a year to buy rare and expensive books as he loves them. Read And Find Out - 2

items.stem: Who is the real culprit in the story ?
items.answer: The real culprit in the story is the lady in red. Think About It

items.stem: Did you begin to suspect, before the end of the story, that the lady was not the person Horace Danby took her to be ? If so, at what point did you realise this and how ?
items.answer: Yes, I started to suspect, before the end of the story, that the lady was not the person Horace Danby took her to be. I realised this when the lady told Horace that she had forgotten the numbers to open the safe and she asked him to break open the safe. She also promised him that she would let him go if only he opened the safe. In fact on one would do this kind of act if she is the real owner of the house.

items.stem: What are the subtle ways in which the lady manages to deceive Horace Danby into thinking she is the lady of the house ? Why doesn’t Horace suspect that something is wrong ?
items.answer: The lady in the red dress was very clever. She was also a thief like Horace. She was also a good planner. She called the dog by its name. She told Horace that she had heard him from the top of the house. She also suggested him to go to some good doctor for the treatment of his hay fever. She threatened to call the police. There was a firmness in her voice. She showed full confidence. Thus Horace was trapped. Since he was a thief, he could not resist and he also did not get time to think. He was caught red haded and was so trapped in that he could not suspect that something was wrong.

items.stem: ‘Horace Danby was good and respectable-but not completely honest’, why do you think this description is apt for Horace ? Why can’t he be categorized as a typical thief ?
items.answer: Horace Danby was unmarried. He was about fifty years old. He was a good-natured man. Therefore, everyone liked him. He was fairly successful in his profession of lock making. As he lived peaceful so he was considered a respectable citizen. But he was not completely honest. He had a keen fondness of rare and expensive books. He needed a great deal of money to buy books. He can’t be described as a typical thief because he committed just one theft every year. Moreover, he would rob only rich people. He never hurt anyone and did not carry any weapons. He was submissive and did not want to go to the prison. So we can justify to say that he was not a typical thief.

items.stem: Horace Danby was a meticulous planner but still he faltered. Where did he go wrong and why ?
items.answer: Horace Danby robbed a safe every year which was enough to last for twelve months. He planned his robbery very meticulously. For two weeks he had been studying the complex situation of the house at Shotover Grange. In the magazine he had read the situation of rooms, electric wires, paths and its garden. He had studied the detailed plan of the drawing room. He had seen the housekeeper hang the key. He had even learnt the name of the dog. The only major mistake had been that he had not even once met the owner of the house. He did not know that the land lady was quite an old lady of sixty. If he had known the lady of the house than the lady in red could not have tricked him. The other mistake was that he had not cut the telephone wires. He also opened the safe without gloves, which left his fingerprint all over. He was easily found and arrested for the jewels robbery. Talk About It

items.stem: Do you think Horace Danby was unfairly punished, or that he deserved what he got ?
items.answer: Horace Danby was a thief but not a typical thief. He had planned robbery at Shotover Grange but not with any bad intention. In this story Horace was punished for the crime which he had not directly done. He had not got the jewels from the Grange Safe. It was his carelessness which had got him caught. He was held culprit and was arrested though he did not get a single jewel. The lady in red posed to be the mistress of the house. She made Horace open the safe. She took all the jewellery in her possession. So it is wrong to say Horace Danby was punished for his crime. He was unfairly punished.

items.stem: Do intentions justify actions ? Would you, like Horace Danby, do something wrong if you thought your ends justified the means ? Do you think that there are situations in which it is excusable to act less than honestly ?
items.answer: Intentions and actions go hand in hand. Intentions and actions are two sides of a coin. If we have good intentions then we will never stoop to do bad even if we are going to be rewarded high. No, I would not do anything wrong like Horace Danby. Even if I am being promised a rich reward, I would not do wrong acts. We know that even a bad company or witnessing a crime can be bad. Honesty is the best policy but still at times we have to keep aside true honesty. Suppose we have not completed our destined task then we have to make some untoward excuses. Such excuses can save us for the moment and save our prestige.

items.stem: “Horace Danby is a thief who was cheated by another thief.” Justify.
items.answer: Horace Danby’s portrayal in “A Question of Trust” reflects the irony of his situation. While he is indeed a thief, his trust is betrayed by another thief, Mr. Cornelius. This deception underscores the complexity of trust and the unpredictable nature of human behavior, even among criminals.

items.stem: How did the lady in red manage to outsmart and out maneuver the other thief, Horace Danby, by robbing the safe without leaving a single fingerprint ?
items.answer: The young lady in red was also a thief but she presented herself as the lady of the house. ... Horace thought that he was opening the safe for the lady of the house. He handed the jewels over to her and went out happily. He had forgotten to wear his gloves and left his fingerprints on the safe.

items.stem: What was Horace Danby’s hobby? How did he manage to fulfil it?
items.answer: Horace Danby had the hobby of collecting rare and expensive books. He managed to fulfill it by robbing a safe every year. Each year he planned carefully just what he would do to steal enough to last for twelve months, and secretly bought the books he loved through an agent.

items.stem: Why did Horace mistake the young lady for the mistress of the house ?
items.answer: The young lady snubbed the house-dog with authority as well as love. She stared at Horace with an imposing air of confidence. She spoke that she had returned just in time. Her manner of speaking and actions made Horace mistake her for the mistress of the house.

items.stem: What made Horace sneeze frequently at the house in Shotover Grange ?
items.answer: Horace had hay fever or was allergic to flowers. There was a great bowl of flowers lying on the table in the house he was supposed to rob in Shotover Grange. Therefore, he felt his nose tickle and he sneezed. He sneezed loudly whenever the smell of flowers came to him again and again in that house.

items.stem: What made Horace believe that the lady was the actual lady of the house ?
items.answer: The young lady had a quiet, firm voice. Entering the room, she walked gracefully to the fireplace and straightened the ornaments there as if she was the owner of the house. Her natural reaction and at ease behaviour, made Horace believe that she was the actual lady of the house.

items.stem: “Society must be protected from men like you.” Do you find this statement ironic ?
items.answer: The lady in the red dress was very shrewd and cunning. She talked about protecting the society from the criminals like Horace when in fact, the lady was the greater culprit. She had come into that house with the same intention as Horace, but had somehow made Horace the culprit when she was the one who had actually stolen the jewels from the house.

items.stem: What do you think is the meaning of the phrase ‘honour among thieves’ ?
items.answer: The phrase ‘honour among thieves’ means that amongst the thieves there ought to be mutual trust, and that thieves do not compromise the theft or activities of other thieves. They are supposed to be honest among fellow criminals and thus, honour each other’s feeling of trust.

items.stem: A small dog was lying in the kitchen. It stirred, made a noise, and moved its tail in a friendly way. (a) What is the name of the dog and where is the kitchen located ? (b) What tact did Horace apply here ?
items.answer: (a) The name of the dog is Sherry. The kitchen was located in a house at Shotover Grange. (b) Horace was very tactful. He had a simple way to keep the dogs quiet. All he had to do was to call them by their right names and show them love.

items.stem: What did Horace Danby wonder about for a moment? What did he think and decide ?
items.answer: On seeing the poor painting in the drawing room, behind which the safe was, Horace Danby wondered for a moment whether he should collect pictures instead of books. But they took up too much room so he soon gave up the idea, as in a small house like his books were better.

items.stem: How often did Horace Danby commit a robbery every year? What did he do with the stolen material?
items.answer: Horace Danby robbed only one safe every year. Each year he planned carefully just what he would do. He stole enough to last him for twelve months and with the rest of the money be bought rare and expensive books, that he loved, through an agent.

items.stem: Why did Horace Danby feel sure of his success in that year’s robbery?
items.answer: Horace Danby felt sure of his success in that year’s robbery as he had been studying rooms, electric wiring, paths and gardens of the house at Shotover Grange for two weeks. He knew that the family was in London and the two servants who lived in the house had gone to watch movie that afternoon.

items.stem: What story did the lady tell Horace to get the jewels?
items.answer: The lady made up a story that before going to London, she promised her husband to take her jewels to their bank; but she left them there in the safe. She wished to put on the jewels to a party that night. Above all she had forgotten the numbers to open the safe. Thus she convinced Horace to open the safe.

items.stem: Why did the police arrest Horace Danby when he had not kept the jewels stolen from Grange safe?
items.answer: The police arrested Horace Danby even when he had not kept the jewels stolen from the Grange Safe because his fingerprints were all over the room. No one believed him when he said that the wife of the owner of the house had asked him to open the safe for her and his story was termed as utter ‘nonsense’.

items.stem: Why would Horace get angry when anyone talked on honour among thieves ?
items.answer: Horace got angry when anyone talked about honour among thieves because being a thief lady in red played a trick on Horace, another thief. She played foul with him and grabbed the entire jewellery. She should have disclosed her identity and shared booty with Horace.

items.stem: What did Horace Danby know about the Shotover Grange House ?
items.answer: Horace Danby had studied the house carefully. He took note of its rooms, electric wiring, paths and garden. He also knew that the family had gone to London. He had seen the servants hanging the keys to the kitchen door and going to pictures.

items.stem: Why did Horace feel sure that year’s robbery at Shotover Grange would be as successful as all the others ?
items.answer: Horace Danby chose the house at Shotover Grange to commit his next burglary. He studied the design of the house carefully. He took note of the rooms, electric wiring, paths and garden. He also knew that the family had gone to London. He had seen the servants hanging the keys to the kitchen door and going to pictures.

items.stem: Why did the lady report to the police though she promised that she would not report to the police?
items.answer: The lady was very clever and shrewd. She promised Horace that she would not report to the police if he helped her in getting the jewels from the safe. Horace broke the safe and helped her. But she didn’t keep her promise as she was also a thief and did not want to get into trouble.

items.stem: Who do you think is the real culprit in the story ‘A Question of Trust’?
items.answer: Obviously the young lady who pretended to be the member of the family was real culprit. She innocently asked Horace to open the safe as she would need the jewels to wear in the party that day. Horace found himself trapped in a tricky situation and could not make out how to escape. He readily opened the safe; unwittingly leaving his fingerprints. He was arrested and nobody believed that the lady of house asked him to open the safe. It seems the young lady outwitted experienced Horace. She cheated and deceived Horace scrupulously.

items.stem: Horace stated that he robbed only those who had a lot of money. Was he really a threat to the society ? Did he lack the qualities of a good citizen ? Discuss the values he needs to imbibe to lead a path of righteousness.
items.answer: I don’t think Horace was a threat to the society. He never threatened anyone and rather stole for a very good reason. He used to rob a safe every year to pursue his hobby of getting rare and expensive books to read. He was not a professional thief. Moreover, he never harmed anyone. He was considered a good and honest citizen by everyone. He was about fifty years old and unmarried. He had all the qualities of a good citizen. He was not a criminal or a typical thief. He did so only to fulfil his need. He was an honest and good man. He believed in the lady’s story and gave away all the jewels to her. If he had been a criminal, he would have killed the lady or would have never handed the jewels to her.

items.stem: Horace Danby requested the lady to forget what she saw. Was Horace afraid of being caught ? Did he lack courage to accept his crime publicly? Explain the values one must imbibe to accept one’s mistake.
items.answer: Yes, Horace Danby was afraid of being caught. He lacked the courage to accept his crime publicly. He was not a professional criminal or thief. He was considered a good and honest man by everyone. He was about fifty years old and unmarried. His house was looked after by a housekeeper. He used to rob only one safe every year to pursue his habit of getting rare and expensive books to read. He used to rob only those who were rich. He had a good reputation in the society and hence did not want anyone to know about his crimes. Although he helped the lady, but was caught by the police for the crime he did not commit. He learnt from his mistake.

items.stem: Describe how Horace Danby planned his robbery of Shotover Grange. Or Horace was the thief who planned his work carefully. Describe what he did before attempting to rob the house at Shotover Grange.
items.answer: A magazine article had described the house Shotover Grange, giving a plan of all the rooms and a picture of the room where the safe was located. The writer had even mentioned that a painting hid the safe. He had studied the house, looking at its rooms, its electric wiring, its paths and gardens for two weeks. He knew that the family lived in London and the two servants who remained in the house had gone to watch movie that afternoon. So he was sure that it was going to be a successful robbery.

items.stem: Describe how the lady in red was a more professional thief than Horace Danby. Or How did the lady in red prove to be smarter and cleverer than Horace Danby?
items.answer: Horace Danby missed to get enough information about all the members of the house. He seems to be too occupied with collecting information about house map, wiring and location of valuable things. Although he was smart enough to know the dog’s actual name but overlooked getting identity of each and every member of the house. Once he was in problem then probably his clever mind gave way to carelessness leading him to open the safe without wearing gloves. On the other hand, the young lady’s confident walk, her act of touching up her make-up and the ease with which she picked cigarette from the right place were enough to make Horace believe that she was lady of the house. Horace was too frightened to think properly so he didn’t suspect anything.

items.stem: Why did Horace choose that house in Shotover Grange for committing a theft ?
items.answer: Horace knew that there were about fifteen thousand pounds worth of jewels in the safe of that house in Shotover Grange. That is why, he decided to commit a theft in that house. He expected to get at least five thousand pounds by selling the jewels one by one, which would make him happy for another year. Horace wanted this money to buy three very interesting books, which were coming for sale the next winter. Moreover, a magazine article had described that house in detail, giving a plan of all the rooms along with the pictures. The magazine had even mentioned that the painting in the room hid the safe. On top of that, the two servants had gone to the movies and the family was in London. Because of all of these circumstances, Horace Danby had chosen that house as the place for committing a theft.

items.stem: Horace Danby represents such people who adopt the wrong ways to fulfil their wishes. What values would you like such people to imbibe to reform themselves?
items.answer: Horace Danby was a successful businessman. He was about fifty years old and a respectable citizen but had a habit that led him to do robberies. Danby loved rare, expensive books and to get them he used to rob a safe every year. Every year he planned carefully just to get what he wanted. Danby adopted wrong ways to fulfil his wishes and hence, later got trapped in a plot by a thief like him. People should imbibe good values. They should learn that hard work is the only key to success. One should work hard to fulfil one’s desires. I think such people should imbibe the values of honesty, responsibility, hard work, dedication and self-confidence in order to reform themselves. One should either curb one’s wishes or try to fulfil them by working hard. There is no shortcut to hard work.

items.stem: “Horace had some hope because she seemed to be amused at meeting him.” Why did Horace feel so? Did he consider the young lady compassionate towards him? Did he find her free from biases? Discuss the values Horace should have imbibe understanding of the person.
items.answer: Horace was a fifty-year-old man who used to rob only to buy rare and expensive. This time he decided to rob Shot over Grange. But as soon as he entered the room, a young lady appeared. She posed to be the lady of the house. She was very confident in her way of mannerism. Then she tried to be polite and nice to him. On hearing her, Horace felt that he had a hope of escaping. He found her a bit compassionate towards him. He was amused at Horace. She acted in quite a subtle manner and showed her sympathy and admiration towards a simple and honest man. He could not judge her ace. She made Horace promise that he would never commit the crime again. Horace should have been clever, shrewd and witty like the lady.
